items.title: Show HN: Receipts, agent skills that make PRDs and metrics cite their evidence
items.summary_1line: Show HN: Receipts, agent skills that make PRDs and metrics cite their evidence
items.editor_note: First tooling item: agent skills that make PRDs and metrics cite their evidence.

editorial.tldr: A loose research cluster, not one event: from Oct 27, arXiv papers on multimodal models gathered around two problems, weak visual perception and answers that lack supporting evidence. Early November added hallucination mitigation, unlearning and knowledge editing, then a human-perception benchmark and an evidence-composing memory system for multimodal agents.
editorial.whats_new: A Show HN project, Receipts, ships agent skills that make PRDs and metrics cite their evidence, a tooling counterpart to the thread's papers on agents that must back answers with support.
editorial.why_it_matters: A correct answer is not necessarily a supported one, and these papers treat evidence retrieval, refusal on thin visual input and distrust of conflicting tool output as things to train and test separately from accuracy.
editorial.take_for_builders: Add a supported-answer check to your agent evals: score whether the cited evidence backs the answer and whether the agent declines when the input is insufficient, separately from answer accuracy.

beats.headline: Correct is not the same as supported
beats.summary: Papers ask agents to retrieve the evidence behind an answer, refuse when an image shows too little, and verify tool outputs that conflict.

beats.headline: Visual perception named as the bottleneck for multimodal reasoning
beats.summary: Training methods reward perception directly or move reasoning into latent space, and a benchmark tests the visual questions people find easy.

beats.headline: Loosely linked: hallucination, unlearning and editing inside multimodal models
beats.summary: These papers share the word "multimodal" with the thread but work on model internals, not agent evidence.

beats.headline: Evidence handling reaches agent memory and agent skills
beats.summary: A memory paper composes evidence across long multimodal histories, and a Show HN project makes product documents cite theirs.

open_questions: Do KG agents trained to retrieve supporting evidence keep their answer accuracy on standard QA benchmarks?
Does conflict-aware evidence verification get tested on production security alert triage, beyond the paper's own evaluation?
How do frontier MLLMs score on HumanSightBench compared with human performance?
Do refusal behaviours for insufficient visual evidence survive post-training, or does fine-tuning erode them?
Does Receipts publish any measurement of how often its cited evidence actually supports the claim?
